related_questions.snippet: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is the most widely used tumor marker for detecting liver cancer. However, other cancers and certain conditions, including pregnancy, hepatitis, and other types of cancer, may also increase AFP levels.

In gastric cancer, biomarkers can reveal details about an individual patient's cancer. Cancer biomarkers include genes, proteins or specific substances produced by the tumor.

related_questions.question: What are the biomarkers for liver cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: Liver cancer biomarkers are measurable substances in the body that indicate the presence or risk of developing liver cancer. These markers can help with diagnosis, prognosis, and predicting treatment response.
snippet_highlighted_words: measurable substances in the body that indicate the presence or risk of developing liver cancer

list.title: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP):
list.snippet: A glycoprotein that is often elevated in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) (the most common type of liver cancer). However, it's not specific to HCC and can be elevated in other conditions like chronic liver disease and pregnancy.

list.title: Des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP):
list.snippet: Also known as PIVKA-II, DCP is another biomarker that is often elevated in HCC. It has shown better specificity than AFP in distinguishing HCC from liver cirrhosis.

list.title: Glypican-3 (GPC3):
list.snippet: GPC3 is a protein that is often overexpressed in HCC and can be used in combination with other markers for diagnosis and prognosis.

list.title: Cytokeratin 19 (CK19):
list.snippet: Co-expression of CK19, AFP, and GPC3 has been found to be a strong indicator of metastasis and poor treatment outcomes.

list.title: Midkine (MDK):
list.snippet: This protein is involved in cell growth and angiogenesis and is elevated in early-stage HCC.

list.title: Exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs):
list.snippet: Specific miRNAs found in exosomes (small vesicles released by cells) can be used as biomarkers for HCC diagnosis and prognosis, including miR-194, miR-17-5p, and miR-106a.

list.title: Gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) mRNA types:
list.snippet: Different types of GGT mRNA (A, B, and C) can be found in the blood and liver tissues of patients with liver cancer. Type B is particularly associated with HCC.

list.title: Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR):
list.snippet: suPAR levels are elevated in HCC and can be used to assess the risk of developing HCC in patients with benign liver disease.

list.title: Deoxycytidine kinase (DCK):
list.snippet: DCK has been identified as a prognostic biomarker in liver cancer, with higher levels indicating a worse prognosis.

list.title: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA):
list.snippet: ctDNA is being explored as a minimally invasive approach for early detection and surveillance of HCC.

list.title: Novel methylation biomarkers:
list.snippet: Tests like the HelioLiver and Oncoguard Liver tests combine methylation biomarkers with other markers (like AFP) and clinical factors to improve early HCC detection.

list.title: Non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs and circRNAs):
list.snippet: These molecules are also being investigated as potential biomarkers for HCC diagnosis and prognosis.

list.title: Traditional Liver Function Tests:
list.snippet: While not specific to cancer, traditional tests like ALT, AST, ALP, GGT, and bilirubin are used to assess overall liver health and can be indicators of liver disease progression.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Biomarkers help identify individuals with HCC, especially in combination with imaging techniques.

list.title: Prognosis:
list.snippet: Biomarkers can help predict the course of the disease, including the likelihood of metastasis and overall survival.

list.title: Treatment Response:
list.snippet: Some biomarkers can help predict how a patient will respond to specific treatments like sorafenib.

list.title: Surveillance:
list.snippet: Biomarkers are used in surveillance programs for individuals at high risk of developing HCC, such as those with cirrhosis.

list.title: Specificity and Sensitivity:
list.snippet: A good biomarker should have high sensitivity (correctly identifying those with the disease) and high specificity (correctly identifying those without the disease).

list.title: Combination of Biomarkers:
list.snippet: Often, a combination of biomarkers is more effective than relying on a single marker.

list.title: Early Detection:
list.snippet: The goal is to identify biomarkers that can detect HCC at an early, curable stage.
